heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P can print Sunlu ASA up to a calculated safe speed of 202 mm/s at 17 mm³/s volumetric flow, though its stock stainless steel nozzle requires no replacement for this non-abrasive material. However, because the P1P features an open-frame design, reliable warp-free printing of ASA requires an external enclosure or draft shield to maintain elevated ambient temperatures.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with liquid glue or PVP glue stick as an interface/release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 17 mm³/s under the Filament Profile to safely prevent underextrusion at high speeds up to 202 mm/s.
Disable the Auxiliary Part Cooling Fan completely (0%) and cap Part Cooling Fan between 0% (min) and 20% (max) to prevent thermal shock and severe delamination.
Enable a 5mm to 8mm outer brim with a 0.0mm brim-object gap to anchor sharp corners on high-aspect-ratio prints without an enclosure.
Set Bed Temperature to 98°C for all layers, operating near the P1P's 100°C limit to maximize bed heat transfer into the low-lying boundary layer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner Lifting and Warping off Bed
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Severe thermal gradient and ambient airflow cooling the higher layers faster than lower layers, shrinking the ASA and peeling it from the plate.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase bed temperature to 98°C, add a 10mm Mouse-Ear or Outer Brim with 0.0mm gap, and cover the open frame of the P1P with a temporary draft tent or enclosure.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or cold cross-drafts preventing molten polymer chain entanglement across successive layers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off the auxiliary side fan completely in the cooling tab, lower maximum part cooling fan to 15-20%, and increase nozzle temperature to 260°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough Surface Finish and Wet Popping Sounds
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Hygroscopic moisture absorption converting to steam within the melt zone, causing voids and uneven extrusion.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the Sunlu ASA spool in a dedicated filament dryer at 70°C for at least 6 to 8 hours before printing, and feed directly from a dry box.

faq.question: Can I print Sunlu ASA on a stock P1P without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Small parts under 50mm can succeed if placed in a draft-free room with high bed temps (98°C) and zero cooling fans, but larger prints will inevitably warp or split without an enclosure.

faq.question: Does Sunlu ASA require upgrading to a hardened steel nozzle on the P1P?
faq.answer: No. Sunlu ASA is an unfilled polymer and is not abrasive, so the stock stainless steel nozzle and extruder gears on the P1P are completely safe from premature wear.

faq.question: Why is the print speed capped at 202 mm/s in this profile?
faq.answer: With a 0.4mm nozzle running standard 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width, the maximum volumetric flow rate of 17 mm³/s equates mathematically to an upper safe velocity ceiling of 202 mm/s.

faq.question: Are the fumes from Sunlu ASA toxic while printing on an open P1P?
faq.answer: ASA releases Styrene and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) during extrusion; because the P1P is open, it must be operated in a well-ventilated room or an enclosed workstation with HEPA/activated carbon filtration.
